title: AlignDefTok: Training-Free Transfer of DefensiveTokens via Embedding-Space Alignment

contributions.purpose: Eliminate the ~16 GPU-hour per-model training cost of DefensiveTokens prompt-injection defenses.
contributions.mechanism: AlignDefTok, the first method for transferring DefensiveTokens between related models (same tokenizer and embedding dimension), enabling defense reuse across model families without retraining.
contributions.evaluation: Achieves 133-285x compute savings versus full DefensiveTokens training while matching native defense performance (0-1.9% ASR on AlpacaFarm).
contributions.source_quote: First, we present the first method for transferring DefensiveTokens between models, enabling defense reuse across model families without per-model retraining.

contributions.purpose: Provide a training-free transfer mechanism that preserves the tokens' critical high-norm property.
contributions.mechanism: Orthogonal Procrustes alignment: compute the optimal rotation matrix from vocabulary embeddings and apply it to the DefensiveTokens, exploiting the norm-preserving property of rotations.
contributions.evaluation: Procrustes transfer achieves 0% attack success rate for the favorable Llama-3.1 to Llama-3 direction with 285x speedup.
contributions.source_quote: Second, we demonstrate that Orthogonal Procrustes alignment provides a training-free, norm-preserving transfer mechanism that achieves 0% ASR for favorable transfer directions.

contributions.purpose: Handle harder transfer directions where pure training-free alignment is insufficient.
contributions.mechanism: tiny-adapt, a lightweight fine-tuning stage that uses Procrustes-transferred tokens as initialization.
contributions.evaluation: Achieves 4x faster convergence for harder transfer directions, reaching 1.9% ASR with 133x speedup.
contributions.source_quote: Third, we introduce tiny-adapt, which leverages Procrustes-transferred tokens as initialization to achieve 4x faster convergence for harder transfer directions.

contributions.purpose: Quantify the overall deployment cost reduction of the transfer approach.
contributions.mechanism: End-to-end comparison of transfer pipeline compute against full DefensiveTokens training on the AlpacaFarm benchmark.
contributions.evaluation: 133-285x compute savings while matching native defense performance (0-1.9% ASR on AlpacaFarm).
contributions.source_quote: Finally, we achieve 133-285x compute savings compared to full DefensiveTokens training while matching native defense performance (0-1.9% ASR on AlpacaFarm).

self_declared_provenance.quote: This suggests that soft prompts trained on one model might transfer to another via embedding space alignment, analogous to cross-lingual word embedding alignment (Schuster et al., 2019).
While effective, these soft prompt defenses require expensive per-model training, motivating our transfer approach.
However, these methods focus on task-specific prompts rather than security-critical defenses, where preserving specific properties like high-norm embeddings is essential.

Our work applies Orthogonal Procrustes alignment to the novel setting of security-focused soft prompt transfer, leveraging its norm-preserving property to maintain defense effectiveness across models.
